question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186105905/plots/f6c02a87892d54ecce9da02ae5259db2f0b88c604d8d42666d0c1f1101f11db9-prompt.png)

Find, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram $ABCD.$

The diagram is not drawn to scale. Use the marked measurements. The dashed diagonal divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The diagonal $\overset{―}{AC}$ divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is twice the area of $△ACB$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186105905/plots/f6c02a87892d54ecce9da02ae5259db2f0b88c604d8d42666d0c1f1101f11db9-solution.png)

 Computing the area of $△ACB,$ we find
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ACB} & =\frac{1}{2}(14)(15)\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & =105\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & ≈90.933,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & =2{A}_{ACB} \\  & =2\cdot 90.933 \\  & ≈181.866.\end{aligned}
$$

So, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram is $182.$
